Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).
Every connected covering of a locally path-connected simply connected space is one-sheeted and isomorphic to the identity covering.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

$$\int_M d\eta=\int_{\partial M}j^*\eta.$$
An empty boundary contributes zero; in dimension one its integral is a finite signed sum of point values.

derivations.claim: Since stability says $I\ne0$, $IJ=0$ forces $J=0$. The real equation is then $|I|^2=\zeta$, so $I$ lies on the circle of radius $\sqrt\zeta$. The $U(1)$ gauge action multiplies $I$ by its phase and leaves scalar $B_1,B_2$ unchanged. It is transitive on that circle with trivial stabilizer; hence the quotient is exactly the unconstrained pair $(B_1,B_2)\in\mathbb C^2$. By [F2], this is the positive-FI stable quotient.

At zero real level, $J=0$ still follows from $I\ne0$ and $IJ=0$, while the real equation becomes $|I|^2=0$. This contradicts $I\ne0$, so the stable zero-level locus is empty. In the positive chamber, $J=0$ makes all of $V$ a nonzero invariant subspace in $\ker J$; the data are not costable. By [F3], their framed sheaves are not locally free.

Let $P\to S^4$ be any smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle. Smooth local connection forms glue by a smooth partition of unity [F5]. Parallel transport from the center of each closed hemisphere along radial segments gives a smooth trivialization: each transported frame solves a linear smooth ODE, and [F5] supplies its smooth dependence on the endpoint. Their transition is a map $g:S^3\to U(1)$. Pulling back the universal cover $\mathbb R\to U(1)$ gives a covering of $S^3$; its connected component through a chosen point is a connected cover, hence is one-sheeted by [F4]. Thus $g$ lifts to $\theta:S^3\to\mathbb R$. Since the covering is a local diffeomorphism and $g$ is smooth, the lift is smooth. The homotopy $\theta_s=(1-s)\theta+s\theta(x_0)$ makes $g$ null-homotopic. Reparameterize this homotopy to be constant near its final parameter and use it on a collar of one hemisphere; this changes that trivialization so the transition is constant and the local frames glue to a global frame. Hence $P$ is trivial. In that frame write the real connection form as $a$ and its curvature as $f=da$, so $df=0$. Then $f\wedge f=d(a\wedge f)$, and Stokes [F6] gives $\int_{S^4}f\wedge f=0$. If it is ASD, $f=-*f$, so $f\wedge f=-f\wedge *f=-|f|^2d\mathrm{vol}$. The zero integral forces $f=0$, and the charge in the Statement is zero. Thus no smooth charge-one $U(1)$ ASD connection exists, and that empty ordinary sector cannot equal the positive-FI quotient $\mathbb C^2$.

citations.quote:
Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

derivations.claim: There is exactly one linear map between any of the zero spaces, so $B_1,B_2,I,J$ are all zero maps. The complex and real equations are equalities between zero endomorphisms. The span of the empty family is $0=V$, and no nonzero subspace of $V$ exists; hence stability and costability hold. The gauge groups have one element, so each quotient consists of one point.

Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2]. No Euler-block or empty-matrix convention changes these calculations.
